prompt: The team can try an installed sensor or a portable service instrument. Which brief gives it an agile intent for the maintainer’s increment?

options.text: Fit the same sensor to every head and reproduce the prototype’s display layout.
options.feedback: This brief selects the equipment and layout before the team has tried either option with a maintainer. It also leaves the success criterion unstated.

options.text: Using the receipt-only adapter, let a maintainer distinguish an observed indication from an unknown one. Demonstrate both cases and let the team choose how.
options.feedback: The brief names the outcome, preserves the interface constraint and gives the team a way to judge success while it explores the design.

options.text: Match every requested phase to the saved T1 trace and accept the service view when the sequence matches.
options.feedback: Matching T1 would check the order of phase requests. The maintainer still needs a way to recognize whether anyone observed the signal head.

prompt: Imagine a Bench 1 test in which the controller logs an amber request and the adapter acknowledges it. The camera record for that command is missing. What should the reviewer record?

options.text: Link the request and receipt to Bench 1 and leave verification of visible amber open.
options.feedback: The log supports receipt for that command. An independent observation of the named head under the test conditions would be needed to decide what it displayed.

options.text: Mark visible amber verified because the implementation decision and both software records agree.
options.feedback: An implementation link identifies how the design realizes a requirement. The two software records stop at command receipt.

options.text: Record that the lamp failed to turn amber because the optical check could not return a result.
options.feedback: The missing camera record leaves the physical state unknown. A dark head or a different color would need an observation of its own.

prompt: The electronics team moves a proposed sensor connector to the other side of the adapter board. What should travel with the change before the team accepts the revised assembly?

options.text: The new board drawing and a passing peak-load test using an emulator of the previous assembly.
options.feedback: The load test exercises the earlier interface assumptions. It leaves clearance, sensor placement and feedback on the revised assembly open.

options.text: The new board revision and the previous lamp observation, since the signal head itself has the same part number.
options.feedback: The board change can affect mounting and the feedback path even with the same head. The old observation belongs to its original assembly.

options.text: The shared requirement and affected board, mounting and firmware revisions, with a fit check and independent indication test on that combination.
options.feedback: These links tell each discipline what changed. The checks can establish whether the connector fits and the diagnostic corresponds to the visible lamp on the revised configuration.
